mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO below 98 for two consecutive months) indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below 98 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both PAYEMS and HOUST signals strengthening household demand and housing activity, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% over three consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which elevates wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a simultaneous decline in consumer spending (proxied by HOUST), indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average and HOUST declines month-over-month.
